transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I guess… I’ve been having thoughts that it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up. I haven’t made any plan to hurt myself or anything, but it’s been on my mind.
How long have you been having these thoughts about not waking up?
I don’t know exactly… it’s been long enough that I keep noticing it. Just that thought that maybe it’d be easier if I didn’t wake up. I haven’t made any plan or anything.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?
Yeah… lately, after that energy kind of wore off, I just felt… empty. Like someone pulled the plug. I’d sit at the table staring at my coffee and feel pretty ashamed.
Have you been enjoying things you usually like to do lately?
Not really. I mean… fishing, going through my records, tailgating, even checking on the home-brew… usually that stuff helps me settle. Lately it just feels like another chore, so I don’t bother much.
Have you noticed any change in your weight recently?
Yeah… a little, I guess. My jeans feel looser. Most days I kind of have to remind myself to eat—supper just looks like too much trouble.
Have you been feeling restless or slowed down lately?
I don’t know… maybe a little slowed down, but I haven’t really paid much attention to it. Nothing I can pin down.
How often have you been having these thoughts about not waking up, are they daily?
Most days, yeah. It’s not like I’m planning anything… I just keep thinking maybe it’d be easier if I didn’t wake up.
Have you been feeling guilty about anything lately?
Yeah… some. After that stretch where I had all that energy, when it wore off I just felt… empty. I’d sit there staring at my coffee and feel ashamed, I guess.
How often do you feel empty or ashamed, is it all the time?
Not all the time… but pretty often. Since that energy kind of dropped off, it’s like I just got unplugged. I’ll sit there with my coffee and just feel… empty, and ashamed, I guess.
Do you feel like you're moving slower than usual?
I don’t know… I haven’t really noticed that. Maybe I’m just tired, but I can’t say I’m moving slower.
How long did that period of high energy last before you started feeling empty and ashamed?
It was… maybe about three weeks. Started after I got fired, and then it kind of went on from there.
Do you feel like you're having trouble sitting still or that you're fidgeting a lot?

Yeah… during that stretch, I guess I was. I’d bounce from job applications to sketching out woodworking stuff to messing with my resume, and I didn’t really sit with one thing very long before starting something else.
Are you still able to find pleasure in the things you used to enjoy?
Not really. Stuff I usually like—fishing, looking through records, tailgating, even checking my home-brew—it’s just… I don’t care much. Feels more like something I have to do than something I enjoy.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in?
Not really. I mean… fishing, records, tailgating, checking the home-brew—those used to help. Now they just feel like chores.
Do you feel like you're having trouble sitting still?
Yeah… I guess so. I wasn’t sitting much. I kept jumping from job applications to woodworking sketches to messing with my resume, then onto something else before I finished.
How long have you been feeling this way, with the emptiness and lack of enjoyment in activities?
About… three months, I guess. Since that crash, it just kind of stuck around.
Would you say these feelings of emptiness and lack of enjoyment have been present for most of the day?
Yeah… most of the day, I’d say. After that energy wore off, it was like someone pulled the plug. I’d just sit there at the table, staring at my coffee, feeling… empty. Ashamed, I guess.
Would you say these feelings of emptiness and lack of enjoyment have been present nearly every day?
Yeah… pretty much nearly every day. Once that energy was gone, I’d just feel drained, sitting there staring at my coffee… empty and kind of ashamed.
Would you describe your feelings of emptiness and lack of enjoyment as mild or more severe?
I’d say mild… not good, but not the worst. Just kind of empty, like the energy was gone and I’d sit there staring at my coffee feeling ashamed.
Would you say these feelings of emptiness and lack of enjoyment have been interfering a lot with your daily life?

Yeah… it has. More than I like to admit. I fell behind on bills, missed some callbacks and appointments. I couldn’t really keep a job search going, even though I needed to. Stuff at home got sloppy too… like I couldn’t just push through it by trying harder.
